frames.narration: A developer's app calls GET /payments with its secret key. The key is sk_live_..., and the app is pinned to API version 2025-03-01 from the day it signed up. The SDK sends the call over TLS.

The gateway hashes the key and finds it in its cache, falling back to the key store. The key belongs to the app acme-web, has the scope payments:read, which this endpoint needs, and is on the free plan, with 4 of 5 monthly calls used in this example.

The call is the fifth of 5, so it is allowed, and the response will carry the headers X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0 and a warning that 80% of the quota was passed. A sixth call would get 429 with a Retry-After header.
The version router sees that this key is pinned to 2025-03-01. It translates the request to the shape the backend uses today and sends it on.
The backend answers in today's shape, where the amount is text. The router translates it back to the old shape the app expects, with the amount as a number, so the app sees what it always saw.

Off the request path, the gateway emits a small usage event: app, endpoint, version, status and latency. A stream job rolls these up by hour into the analytics store, which feeds the billing and the dashboard.

Meanwhile an engineer proposes a change that removes the status field. The contract check diffs the new OpenAPI description against the published one, classifies the removal as breaking, and fails the build, because the usage data shows that apps still read this field.
So the change goes out as a new version, 2026-03-01. The pinned app keeps getting the old shape through the router, and its owner sees a notice in the portal with a sunset date several months away.
